Subject: Invoice visibility after user data removal

Hi Marcus,

Hope you're well. We're reviewing our internal policies and have a compliance question for Redwood. One of our end users recently asked BrightFinance to erase their personal data under a local privacy law. The request affects records tied to that user and some associated billing items.

Can you confirm what Redwood preserves for accounting and tax purposes versus what gets removed for a user-driven deletion? Specifically:
- Will BrightFinance still be able to access invoice PDFs and transaction line items for the relevant month?
- Do you retain a ledger or export that shows usage/charges if the underlying user identifier is erased?
- If personal identifiers are scrubbed, do line-item amounts and timestamps remain available for audits?

We need a short explanation for our finance team and an attestable workflow we can include in our audit packet. Any attachments or evidence we can point the auditors to (e.g., invoice PDFs, signed receipts, export snapshots) would help.

Thanks,

Marcus / Marissa — here is the guidance from Finance + Compliance. I'm keeping it high level so you can share with procurement; if BrightFinance wants a formal attestation, we can prepare a short statement on letterhead.

Summary (short):
- Accounting and tax obligations require us to retain transactional evidence (invoices, summarized ledger entries, tax receipts) for statutory periods (US federal and state tax rules typically 3–7 years depending on jurisdiction). Those artifacts are retained regardless of a downstream user data erasure request.
- We do not preserve PII when a DSR erasure is processed. Instead we maintain accounting records that have had identifying fields redacted or replaced with internal non-reversible tokens. Line-item amounts, timestamps, invoice numbers, tax amounts, and payment status are preserved to support audits.

Technical/operational notes:
- Invoice PDFs: We retain invoice PDFs as immutable artifacts tied to an invoice id. When a user deletion is enacted, the invoice PDF is retained but any embedded user PII is redacted where feasible. The PDF file metadata still contains invoice id, date, and totals.
- Billing ledger / exports: We maintain an accounting ledger (compressed event log and monthly snapshots). For DSR erasures we run a transformation that removes or hashes user identifiers (email, user id) but keeps financial columns (amount, currency, line-item codes, timestamp). The export snapshot we can provide for audits will contain non-PII bookkeeping columns + the invoice id.
- Proof for auditors: We can provide redacted invoice PDFs and a CSV snapshot (billing snapshot) with the invoice id, amounts, dates, tax breakdowns, and payment status. We can also provide an audit trail showing when the DSR was received and the deletion job run.

Exceptions / legal hold:
- If there's an active legal hold or regulatory investigation, we will not run erasure for records under hold — those records will be preserved until the hold is lifted. Finance should notify Legal immediately if auditors request preservation beyond the normal retention window.

Actionable items for Marcus to send to BrightFinance:
1) Confirm we will attach redacted invoice PDF and a billing snapshot CSV for the affected month.
2) Offer the option to assert a limited legal hold if their auditors need the full PII-backed records (we'll need a signed request and legal review).
3) Provide a HubSpot ticket and DocuSign link for any attestation they require.

Attachments we can include:
- redwood_billing_snapshot_20270625.csv (billing columns only)
- template_redacted_invoice.pdf (example redaction)

Let me know if you want specific language for procurement.

-Neha

- Remove/Redact: end-user personal identifiers (email, name, user id) in both the PDFs and ledger exports unless a legal hold is submitted.
